A business with few workers and limited capital and turnover; it may be formal or informal.
Measures that protect workers from injury and disease caused by their work.
Personal protective equipment: masks, goggles, gloves, overalls, boots, ear protectors, hard hats.
Siyaso and Magaba in Mbare: small workshops making scotch carts, stoves, buckets and spare parts from scrap metal.
Formal job losses (ESAP in the 1990s, factory closures), urban population growth, low entry costs, demand for cheap goods.
Jobs and income, cheap goods and services, apprenticeship training, recycling, import substitution, links with formal firms.
No credit or collateral, insecure premises, power cuts, competition from imports, council raids, unsafe conditions.
The National Social Security Authority runs workers' compensation and promotes occupational safety and health in Zimbabwe.
